title: Atomic structure and the periodic table - 123 school
heading: Atomic structure and the periodic table
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What charge do a proton, a neutron and an electron have?
questions.a: Proton positive (1+), neutron no charge, electron negative (1−)

questions.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom?
questions.a: In the nucleus

questions.q: What is the atomic number?
questions.a: The number of protons

questions.q: What is the mass number?
questions.a: The number of protons plus the number of neutrons

questions.q: How do you calculate the number of neutrons?
questions.a: Mass number minus atomic number

questions.q: A chlorine atom has mass number 35 and atomic number 17. How many neutrons does it have?
How many electrons does a neutral atom have?
questions.a: The same as the number of protons

questions.q: What are isotopes?
questions.a: Atoms of the same element with a different number of neutrons

questions.q: What is the unit of atomic mass?
questions.a: u

questions.q: Why is the atomic mass in BINAS table 99 not a whole number?
questions.a: It is an average of the masses of the isotopes

questions.q: What are the rows and the columns of the periodic table called?
questions.a: Rows: periods. Columns: groups.

questions.q: What do elements in the same group have in common?
questions.a: The same number of valence electrons

questions.q: What do elements in the same period have in common?
questions.a: The same number of shells containing electrons

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons in the K, L and M shells?
What are valence electrons?
questions.a: The electrons in the outer shell

questions.q: What is the electron arrangement of oxygen (atomic number 8)?
What is the electron arrangement of chlorine (atomic number 17)?
How many valence electrons does an element in group 17 have?
What is a noble gas configuration?
questions.a: An outer shell that is completely filled

questions.q: Which group contains the noble gases?
questions.a: Group 18

questions.q: What are the elements in group 1 (except hydrogen) and in group 17 called?
questions.a: Group 1: alkali metals. Group 17: halogens.

questions.q: What is an ion?
questions.a: A charged particle (an atom that has gained or lost electrons)

questions.q: What happens when sodium (atomic number 11) becomes a Na<sup>+</sup> ion?
questions.a: It loses 1 electron

questions.q: How many electrons does an O<sup>2-</sup> ion have (atomic number 8)?
Which ions do metals form and which ions do non-metals form?
questions.a: Metals form positive ions, non-metals form negative ions

questions.q: How many protons, neutrons and electrons does an atom of Na-23 have? (atomic number 11)
questions.a: Protons = atomic number = 11; neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12; electrons = 11 (the atom is neutral)

questions.q: How many protons, neutrons and electrons does the ion Mg<sup>2+</sup> with mass number 24 have? (atomic number 12)
questions.a: Protons = 12; neutrons = 24 − 12 = 12; electrons = 12 − 2 = 10

questions.q: What is the electron arrangement of aluminium? (atomic number 13)
Which ion does a calcium atom form? (atomic number 20)
questions.a: Calcium is in group 2: the atom loses 2 electrons and becomes Ca<sup>2+</sup>

questions.q: How many electrons does the ion S<sup>2-</sup> have? (atomic number 16)
questions.a: 16 + 2 = 18 electrons

questions.q: An atom has the electron arrangement K = 2, L = 8, M = 5. In which group and period is the element?
questions.a: 3 shells means period 3; 5 valence electrons means group 15 (phosphorus)

questions.q: Boron occurs as B-10 (19.9%) and B-11 (80.1%). Calculate the average atomic mass, using the mass numbers as the masses.
Which ion charge do elements from group 2 and from group 16 form?
questions.a: Group 2: 2+ (lose two electrons); group 16: 2- (gain two electrons)

questions.q: How do you calculate the average atomic mass of an element with several isotopes?
questions.a: Multiply the mass of each isotope by its percentage, add them up and divide by 100 (weighted average)

questions.q: How many shells and how many valence electrons does potassium have? (atomic number 19)
questions.a: 4 shells (K = 2, L = 8, M = 8, N = 1) and 1 valence electron
